scenes.name: Nueva psicodelia y big music: Echo & the Bunnymen y U2
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En lugar de descender a lo oscuro, elevarse hacia la luz. Liverpool, que no tuvo punk clásico ni postpunk experimental, quería que la música fuera «una fiesta» (Bill Drummond, Zoo): el club Eric's, las bandas fantasma (The Crucial Three, Big in Japan), Wah! Heat, The Teardrop Explodes de Julian Cope. Echo & the Bunnymen, con el minimalismo aprendido de Television y la voz de Ian McCulloch, graban Crocodiles y Heaven Up Here, respuesta luminosa a Closer, y heredan el público huérfano de Joy Division; Ocean Rain los vuelve estrellas pop. U2, «punk positivo» cristiano y pacifista, guitarra de The Edge como sintetizador, quiere ocupar el lugar de Curtis: War (1983), «Sunday Bloody Sunday» en MTV, The Unforgettable Fire con Eno. Alrededor, la «big music» celta de Simple Minds, The Waterboys, Big Country y la neopsicodelia de The Blue Orchids.

podcast.title: Anger at Bono Post-Live Aid (July 13, 1985)
podcast.body: After U2's Live Aid performance, The Edge was "furious" with Bono for his on-stage "grandstanding" and failure to adhere to the band's plan, which resulted in them not playing their hit "Pride (In the Name of Love)." "The Edge, Larry and Adam were furious with Bono's grandstanding and his inability to stick with the plan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 1

podcast.title: Captive (1986) - Soundtrack Collaboration
podcast.body: The Edge composed the soundtrack for the movie *Captive* and collaborated with Sinead O'Connor, getting her to sing the movie's theme, "Heroine," and also giving her a songwriting credit. "And suddenly, she found herself in the studio with the edge who was composing the soundtrack for a movie called Captive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Guitar Parts for "One Tree Hill"
podcast.body: The Edge contributed his distinctive guitar parts to the U2 song "One Tree Hill." These parts, combined with Bono's lyrics and the efforts of Toronto musicians, helped finalize the track dedicated to roadie Greg Carroll. "With Bono's lyrics, the edges guitar parts and contributions from three Toronto musicians at Grant Avenue Studios in Hamilton, the song was finished."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death (December 3, 2015)
xref.body: Scott Weiland was found dead on his tour bus in a hotel parking lot near Minneapolis on December 3, 2015. He was known for his long history of drug and drinking habits and self-destructive behavior, always seemingly on the verge of a fatal incident. "When Scott Wyland was found dead on his tour bus in the parking lot of a hotel, not far from Minneapolis, Wyland was always dancing on the edge of something fatal with his drug and drinking habits and the spurts of self-destructive behavior."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: CC Deville's Alleged Contact with U2
xref.body: An uncorroborated rumor suggests that Poison guitarist CC Deville was contacted by U2 in the early 1990s to act as their backup guitarist for the *Achtung Baby* album and the Zoo TV tour. Deville was allegedly flattered but turned down the offer, citing a desire "not to compromise his musical integrity." Furthermore, alleged quotes from Bono and The Edge are presented, praising Deville's guitar work and crediting Poison as inspiration for U2's visual choices during the *Achtung Baby* era.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Collaborations and Film Role (Late 1980s)
xref.body: Between the ages of 16 and 20, Sinead's career accelerated rapidly. She co-wrote and recorded with The Edge, toured with INXS and David Bowie (with Andy Rourke and Mike Joyce of The Smiths in her band), had songs placed in movies, and starred in a Northern Irish film called *Hasha-Veibaby*. "She performed on David Letterman, participated in more collaborations with other artists, had her songs placed in movies. And she starred in a movie from Northern Ireland called Hasha-Veibaby."

xref.title: Early Dark Irish Group
xref.body: This Irish group featured guitarist Dick Evans, whose baby brother Dave would later adopt the name The Edge and end up in U2. The Virgin Prunes were part of the early wave of artists making dark music that fed into the goth movement. "And then there was an Irish group called The Virgin Prunes featuring a guitarist named Dick Evans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Evolving Musical Structure
xref.body: While known for their experimental and noisy approach, Sonic Youth's music developed more structure as the 1980s progressed. Despite this evolution, they consistently pushed the boundaries of musical expression. "Although Sonic Youth's music became more structured as the 80s progressed, there was always the sense that they were pushing the edge of the musical envelope."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Final Days Before Disappearance
xref.body: Following the holiday season, Richie ceased writing in his diary on January 17, 1995, just three days after his beloved cocker spaniel, Snoopy, died at age 17, leaving him inconsolable. Coupled with band tensions and a relationship breakdown, he seemed to be on the verge of a crisis. He made four trips to a Cardiff bank machine, withdrawing £200 each time, spending money on mundane items like comic books, books, VHS movies, and flowers for his mother, whom he visited one last time. "By the end of January, Richie was teetering on the edge of something really, really bad. He also seemed to be up to something."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Forming U2 – The Bulletin Board Note
xref.body: At age 15, frustrated with formal lessons, Larry Mullen pinned a note to the bulletin board at Mount Temple High School in Dublin. The note sought out other musicians who had "wasted money" on guitars. This initiative led him to approach Adam Clayton, and later attracted Dave and Dick Evans (The Edge) and Paul Husson (Bono), leading to the band's first rehearsal in Larry's kitchen in the autumn of 1976. "one day when he was 15 Larry pinned a note to the bulldozen board at Mount Temple High School in Dublin The note said money wasted on a drum kit Were there others out there who had wasted money on guitars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hired at The Edge
xref.body: Following George Stroumboulopoulos's advice, Ben emailed Phil Evans at The Edge radio station for a job interview. Despite having no high school or radio/television education, he convinced Phil Evans to hire him by promising to work harder than anyone else. "And he said, you know, when did you graduate from radio television? I'm like, I didn't. He's like, well, when did you graduate from high school? Like, I didn't. And he said, well, why should I give you the job? And I was like, because I'll work harder than anybody else. I'll come here early and I'll stay late every day. I promise. ... And as I was walking home, he called me and said, you start Monday."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence on Contemporary Artists
xref.body: The album *Loveless* had a profound and widespread impact, blowing away musicians such as Trent Reznor, Billy Corgan, Robert Smith, Courtney Love, and The Edge of U2. Its influence far exceeded its commercial sales, cementing its status as a seminal work in alternative music and being frequently cited by contemporary bands as an inspiration. "Everyone from Trent Resner to Billy Corgan to Robert Smith to Courtney Love to the edge of YouTube were blown away by what they heard on that album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Inventor of Infinite Sustain Guitar
xref.body: Michael Brook, hailing from a family of scientists, invented and constructed the "infinite sustain guitar" in Chinatown, Toronto. He developed this instrument after experimenting with E-Bows and built three units: one for himself, one for The Edge of U2, and one for Daniel Landwom. "the infinite sustain guitar was born in Chinatown in Toronto by an old friend, a Michael Brook."

xref.title: Pioneer of Unconventional Music
xref.body: Iggy Pop is recognized for insisting on doing the unconventional, pushing the envelope to an extent that few have since matched. His influence created a "straight line" from his early work through the punk of the 70s, indie rock of the 80s, grunge of the 90s, to today's punk and underground music, demonstrating how "undiluted, straight from the rock and roll" should be done. "Iggy was one of those guys who insisted on doing the unconventional. Who pushed the envelope so far that few people since have managed to stand that far out on the edge."

xref.title: Presidential Suite Incident (Unknown Year)
xref.body: Michael Jackson dangled his son, Prince Michael the Second, over the edge of a balcony at the presidential suite of the Hotel Elden Kepenski in Berlin. The suite reportedly cost around $16,000 a night at the time. "Michael Jackson dangled his son, Prince Michael the second over the edge."

xref.title: Pushing Musical Boundaries
xref.body: As the 1980s progressed, Sonic Youth's music became more structured, but they consistently pushed the edge of the musical envelope. A deal with Black Flag's indie label, SST Records, helped them spread their influence throughout North America. "Although Sonic Youth's music became more structured as the 80s progressed, there was always the sense that they were pushing the edge of the musical envelope and thanks to a deal with black flags, indie label, SST records, they were able to spread their influence throughout North America."

xref.title: Son of The Edge and Morleigh Steinberg
xref.body: Levi Evans is the only son of Dave "The Edge" Evans and Morleigh Steinberg, who was known as the "Mysterious Ways" dancer during U2's Zoo TV tour. He has an older sister named Sean and three stepsisters. "Levi is the edges only son. He has an older sister named Sean and three step sisters from the Edge's first marriage."
